ACDM: Airport Collaborative Decision Making - A framework in which airport operators, airlines, ground handlers, ATC, and other stakeholders share real-time operational data to optimize aircraft turnaround, reduce delays, and improve overall airport efficiency and predictability.
DCL: Departure Clearance - A data link service that enables controllers to issue departure clearances (including route, altitude, and frequency assignments) to pilots via digital text rather than voice radio, reducing communication errors and frequency congestion.
ADP: ATFM Daily Plan - A daily plan developed by the Air Traffic Flow Management unit that outlines expected traffic demand, capacity constraints, and flow management measures to balance traffic flow with available airspace and airport capacity.
CDM: Collaborative Decision Making Meeting - A regular meeting where aviation stakeholders (airlines, ATC, airport authorities) coordinate and share information to optimize air traffic flow and resource utilization.
COBT: Calculated Off-Block Time - The calculated time at which an aircraft is expected to begin moving (push back from the gate), as determined by the ATFM slot allocation process.
CTO: Calculated Time Over - The calculated time at which an aircraft is expected to cross a specific waypoint or fix, as part of the ATFM slot coordination process.
CTOT: Calculated Take-Off Time - The time allocated by the ATFM system at which an aircraft is expected to take off, used to manage traffic flow and reduce delays at congested airports.
D: Downward - An indicator used in RVR (Runway Visual Range) reports to show that the visibility has been decreasing during the previous 10-minute period.
ELDT: Estimated Landing Time - The estimated time at which an aircraft is expected to land at its destination airport, used for arrival sequencing and gate assignment planning.
ETOT: Estimated Take-Off Time - The estimated time at which an aircraft is expected to depart, used in flight planning and ATFM slot coordination.
FDR: Flight Data Recorder - An electronic recording device installed in aircraft that continuously captures flight parameters (altitude, airspeed, heading, etc.) for accident investigation and flight analysis purposes.
GRID: Grid Point Data - Processed meteorological data presented at regular grid points for aviation weather forecasting and analysis.
IC: Ice Crystals - Very small ice crystals suspended in the atmosphere, often appearing as a type of precipitation or cloud phenomenon that can affect visibility and aircraft operations.
KST: Korean Standard Time - The standard time zone used in South Korea (UTC+9), used for all aviation operations and flight planning within Korean airspace.
LSQ: Line Squall - A line of thunderstorms or severe weather along a squall line, typically associated with a cold front, posing hazards to aviation including strong winds, turbulence, and reduced visibility.
MINT: Minutes In Trail - A traffic spacing method where aircraft are separated by a specified number of minutes to manage arrival flows and maintain safe separation.
MIT: Miles In Trail - A traffic spacing method where aircraft are separated by a specified distance in nautical miles to manage arrival flows and ensure safe separation.
OTLK: Outlook - Used in SIGMET (Significant Meteorological Information) messages for volcanic ash and tropical cyclone events to indicate forecast conditions expected beyond the standard validity period.
RX: Receiver - A radio receiver device used in aviation communications and navigation systems to receive signals from ground stations, satellites, or other aircraft.
U: Upward - An indicator used in RVR (Runway Visual Range) reports to show that the visibility has been increasing during the previous 10-minute period.
AMSS: Aeronautical Mobile Satellite Service - A satellite-based communication service that provides voice and data links between aircraft and ground stations for air traffic control and operational communications.
ANC: Aeronautical Chart 1:500,000 - A small-scale aeronautical chart used for visual flight rule (VFR) navigation, covering an area at a scale of 1:500,000, typically followed by the chart name or title.
ANCS: Aeronautical Navigation Chart - Small Scale - A small-scale aeronautical chart designed for long-range navigation, providing an overview of airspace structure, navigation aids, and other essential flight information.
AT: At - A prefix used in aviation weather forecasts (such as TAF) to indicate the specific time at which a weather change is forecast to occur.
BLDU: Blowing Dust - Dust raised by wind to a height of 2 meters or more above the ground, reducing visibility. Part of ICAO weather phenomena codes (BLSA = blowing sand, BLSN = blowing snow).
ENRC: Enroute Chart - An aeronautical chart designed for navigation during the enroute phase of flight, showing airways, navigation aids, airspace boundaries, and other information needed for cross-country flight.
GMC: Ground Movement Chart - An aeronautical chart depicting airport taxiways, aprons, and movement areas in detail, used for ground navigation of aircraft between runways and gates.
TX: Transmitter - A radio transmitter device used in aviation for communications and navigation, broadcasting signals from aircraft or ground stations.
VC: Vicinity of the Aerodrome - A descriptor used in meteorological reports to indicate weather phenomena occurring near (but not at) the aerodrome, typically within 8 to 16 kilometers, followed by the weather code (e.g., VCFG = vicinity fog).
A: Amber - A color used in aviation lighting and signaling systems, often indicating caution or specific operational status in aerodrome lighting and visual aids.
ARFOR: Area Forecast - A meteorological forecast covering a specified geographical area, issued in aeronautical meteorological code for aviation flight planning and weather briefing purposes.
B: Blue - A color used in aviation lighting and signaling systems, including taxiway lighting, visual docking guidance, and meteorological status indicators.
C: Degrees Celsius (Centigrade) - The standard unit of temperature measurement used in aviation meteorology for reporting outside air temperature, dew point, and other temperature-related parameters.
CIT: Near or Over a Large Town - A location qualifier used in aviation weather reports and forecasts to indicate that a weather phenomenon is occurring near or over a significant urban area.
DENEB: Fog Dispersal Operations - Operations involving equipment and procedures to disperse fog at an aerodrome to improve visibility and enable flight operations. Note: This code has been deleted from current usage.
E: East or Eastern Longitude - A cardinal direction and geographic coordinate indicator used in aviation for navigation, route planning, and position reporting.
ER: Here or Herewith - A term used in NOTAM and aviation text communications to indicate the current location or document being referenced.
F: Fixed - A designation used in aviation to indicate something that is stationary or permanently established, such as a fixed navigation aid or fixed-wing aircraft.
G: Green - A color used in aviation lighting systems, including threshold lights, centerline lights, and status indicators for various airport systems.
L: Locator or Left - A locator is a low-power radio navigation aid used for non-precision approaches. When preceded by a runway designation number, 'L' identifies the left runway of a parallel pair.
LTT: Landing Teletypewriter - A dedicated teletypewriter circuit used for transmitting landing information and aeronautical meteorological data between aviation facilities.
MAS: Manual AI Simplex - A manual, single-direction (simplex) communication mode using AI (perhaps referring to a specific teletype or data circuit configuration in aviation communications).
N: North or Northern Latitude - A cardinal direction and geographic coordinate indicator. Also used in RVR reports to indicate no significant change (Nil change) in visibility during the previous 10 minutes.
PE: Ice Pellets - A form of precipitation consisting of transparent or translucent ice particles (sleet), which can affect aircraft performance and runway conditions.
R: Red - A color used in aviation lighting and signaling. Also used as a prefix to identify Restricted Areas (followed by the area number) in airspace classification.
RAFC: Regional Area Forecast Center - A meteorological center responsible for preparing and issuing area forecasts for a specific region to support aviation operations.
RITE: Right - A direction of turn or position, used in air traffic control instructions and aviation phraseology to indicate a right-hand turn or right-side positioning.
ROFOR: Route Forecast - A meteorological forecast issued in aeronautical code for a specific air route, providing information on winds, temperatures, weather phenomena, and other conditions along the flight path.
S: South or Southern Latitude - A cardinal direction and geographic coordinate indicator used in aviation navigation, route planning, and position reporting.
SAP: As Soon As Possible - An abbreviation used in aviation communications and NOTAM text to indicate urgency in completing a requested action or complying with an instruction.
